transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-11 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~64 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Neha Rao (Redwood SE), Evan Brooks (Redwood Product), Lena Park (Saffron Head of Partnerships), Omar Farouk (Saffron Lead Integration), Priya Nair (Saffron Cloud Architect), Derek Wu (Saffron SRE)

Auto-generated summary (may be incomplete): Initial technical intro for onramp partnership. Discussed integration patterns for Saffron's managed SaaS customers, NVidia/GPU sizing, VPC networking, auth and KMS, and pilot scope.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro from the Redwood side, I'm Maya, I'm the AE on this. With me Daniel and Neha from SE, Evan from product.
[00:12] Lena: Hi, Lena here, thanks. We're excited to talk about the onramp - we have a bunch of customers that want a turnkey integration to Redwood's serving runtime.
[00:20] Omar: afternoon, yeah, quick background: Saffron runs a multi-tenant SaaS for legal document automation, heavy embeddings, and some generation. We're evaluating partners for a managed GPU onramp so we don't manage weights ourselves.
[00:35] Daniel (Redwood): Nice. Can you give a bit of the current stack - cloud provider, networking, and any data residency constraints?
[00:43] Priya: We're mostly on GCP in us-central1, some EMEA customers on region-eu-west. We do VPC peering with customer networks for higher tiers, and some customers require keys stay in their KMS / HSM.
[00:55] Neha: Got it. On the Redwood side we support three deployment modes - hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private VPC/on-prem. For the onramp use case most partners start with a hybrid: hosted control plane + private data plane via VPC.
[01:12] Derek: When you say private data plane, what's the auth flow? We want RBAC and SSO integration with our IdP.
[01:18] Evan: We can integrate SAML/SO with SSO and support service-account level RBAC; we also offer audit logs and per-token tracing. For KMS you can either bring your own and we call it through a customer KMS endpoint, or use Redwood KMS with HSM-backed keys.
[01:32] Omar: Any gotchas around egress? We have strict egress controls and a whitelisting policy.
[01:37] Daniel: We usually recommend a minimal set of egress rules - outbound to our control plane endpoints on port 443, and depending on model hosting we may need access to container registries or model stores. For private deployments we can also run fully inside your VPC with no outbound egress if needed, that's the on-prem-like option.
[01:55] Lena: Cost / latency talk: our customers care about p95 latency under 300ms for chat flows, and cost sensitivity is high. How do you recommend balancing Dedicated vs Hosted?
[02:06] Neha: For that latency/p95 target, dedicated pools with pinned GPUs and continuous batching tuned to short sequences works best. Hosted is cheaper and faster to onboard but you'd see more variability; dedicated gives predictable p95 and throughput. We can also do autoscale bursts for peak traffic.
[02:22] Priya: Can you share GPU shapes or quantization profiles you recommend? We're also trying to avoid hallucination regressions when quantizing.
[02:30] Daniel: Sure - for generation-heavy workloads we suggest A10G or A100 variants depending on model size. For cost-sensitive embedding loads we've had success with 8-bit quantized M-class models; we have internal quant profiles but we warn about QA and evals because quant can change output distribution. We'll provide recommended profiles and benchmark numbers.
[02:49] Omar: Is the KV cache shared across tenants or per-tenant? We worry about cache leakage and multi-tenancy safety.
[02:56] Evan: It's per-tenant logical caches; the runtime isolates KV caches between customer contexts. There are periodic mis-transcriptions in logs sometimes where names get swapped, but the isolation is enforced.
[03:08] Lena: Security/compliance asks - SOC2, iso, penetration testing reports?
[03:13] Maya: We are SOC2 Type II compliant and have SOC2 report packages for customer review. We also support annual pentest reports; we'll include redacted reports in the security pack.
[03:22] Priya: KMS flow detail: if we bring our own KMS, how does Redwood talk to it? Direct RPC or via a proxy?
[03:29] Neha: We support both. Typically we establish a VPC peering and either use a private endpoint to call your KMS or you deploy a small key-proxy container managed by you. We'll document the options.
[03:41] Derek: For pilot benchmarks, what test harness do you recommend? We have a set of production prompts and embeddings workload, want representative mix.
[03:48] Daniel: We'll provide a pilot runbook: steady-state qps tests, tail-latency tracking (p50/p95/p99), cost per 1k tokens, and embedding throughput. We'll also run a small A/B against your current provider if you want.
[04:02] Omar: That A/B would be useful. Also need a runbook for outages and failovers - our SLAs require 99.9 for critical ops.
[04:11] Evan: Redwood supports graceful degradation and automatic fallback to lighter models or alternate regions. We'll share typical rollback strategies and TF scripts for canary rollouts.
[04:22] Lena: Competitors - some of our teams already talked to NimbusGrid and AuroraCompute; they offered a marketplace integration but lacked private VPC option which is a blocker for some customers.
[04:34] Maya: Noted. We try to position the private data plane as a differentiator.
[04:38] Priya: Networking specifics - do you support GCP Private Service Connect or only VPC peering?
[04:44] Daniel: We support Private Service Connect, VPC peering, and interconnect depending on provider. For GCP we frequently use PSC for stable private endpoints. We'll include sample Terraform snippets.
[04:58] Omar: What about observability? We need per-customer cost breakdown for chargeback and token-level traces.
[05:05] Neha: Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdown, per-model dashboards, and trace hooks; we can also ship logs to your SIEM or create a dedicated Prometheus endpoint.
[05:18] Derek: Any sample SLA language you can share? Our legal team will want to see terms for uptime and incident response.
[05:24] Maya: We'll share a standard SLA and a draft SOW. For onramp partnerships we usually start with a 90-day pilot then convert to dedicated reserved capacity if performance is good.
[05:36] Priya: How do you handle model updates and rollouts? We need version pinning for legal/regulatory reasons.
[05:42] Evan: Customers can pin model versions and there's built-in rollout policies - canary, A/B test, or immediate. We also support immutable model snapshots used for audits.
[05:52] Omar: Ok let's scope the pilot: one week of benchmark with our set of prompts, 2 dedicated A10G GPUs during the pilot, routing via PSC, and a small A/B run against current provider. Is that feasible?
[06:03] Daniel: Yes that's reasonable as a starting point. We'll create a runbook and share infrastructure cost estimates.
[06:11] Lena: On commercials, what's the pricing structure for a partner onramp? Flat fee plus usage? Marketplace rev share?
[06:18] Maya: Usually options: usage-based for hosted, committed monthly for dedicated, and partner revenue share models for reseller-like flows. We'll propose 3 pricing bands in the draft SOW.
[06:28] Derek: One more thing - data retention and delete on request. Some customers require full deletions within 30 days.
[06:34] Neha: We support configurable retention policies and can implement customer-triggered deletion flows; we'll note the operational steps.
[06:42] (brief cross-talk, muted)
[06:48] Action recap: Maya: we'll send the security pack and VPC template; Daniel will produce the pilot runbook and recommended GPU shapes; Neha will outline quantization guidance and eval caveats; Saffron to share infra diagram and perf targets.
[06:58] Lena: Sounds good, timeline looks workable. Can we commit to the pilot week by next call?
[07:03] Maya: Yes, we'll target the first week of April, send calendar invite once Saffron shares preferred dates.
[07:10] Omar: Thanks, appreciate the level of detail. Looking forward to the SOW.
[07:15] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and SOW.

End of transcript.
